chunks: Ahmad ibn Muhammad al-Haysam al-Ajali, Ahmad ibn al-Hasan al-Qattan, Muhammad ibn Ahmad al-Sin'ani, al-Husayn ibn Ibrahim ibn Ahmad ibn Hisham al-Mokattib, Abdullah ibn Muhammad al-Sa'iq, and Ali ibn Abdullah al-Varraq (may God be pleased with them) narrated that Abul Abbas Ahmad ibn Yahya ibn Zakariya al-Qattan said: Bakr ibn Abdullah ibn Habib narrated to us, Tamim ibn Buhlool narrated to us, Abu Muawiyah narrated to us, from al-A'mash, from Ja'far ibn Muhammad (peace be upon him).

He said: These are the religious decrees for whoever wishes to adhere to them, and God guides him: Spreading the ablution as God the Exalted commanded in His Speaking Book: washing the face and hands to the elbows, wiping the head and feet to the ankles, once or twice is permissible. Ablution is only broken by urine, wind, sleep, feces, and major impurity. Whoever wipes over his slippers has contradicted God, His Messenger, and His Book, his ablution is not complete, and his prayer is not accepted. The ritual baths include: bath of major impurity, menstruation, bath of the dead, bath of one who touched the dead after it cools, bath of one who washed the dead, bath of Friday, bath of the two Eids, bath of entering Mecca, bath of entering Medina, bath of visitation, bath of Ihram, bath of the day of Arafat, bath of the 17th night of Ramadan, bath of the 19th night of Ramadan, bath of the 21st and 23rd nights thereof. As for the obligatory bath, it is the bath of major impurity, and the bath of major impurity and menstruation are one.

key_terms.إِسْبَاعُ الْوُضُوءِ: Spreading/completing the ablution (washing all parts thoroughly)
key_terms.الْجَنَابَةُ: Major ritual impurity (caused by sexual intercourse or ejaculation)
key_terms.الْخُفَّانِ: The two slippers/leather socks (wiping over them instead of washing feet)
key_terms.شَرَائِعُ الدِّينِ: Religious decrees or fundamental rites of worship

ai.seo_question: What are the specific rules for ritual ablution and the occasions requiring ritual bathing in Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: Attributed to Imam Ja'far al-Sadiq, this hadith serves as a concise manual of ritual purity, emphasizing the completeness of ablution and the specific invalidators such as sleep and flatulence. It highlights the Shia jurisprudential view that wiping over shoes (khuffayn) is insufficient for valid prayer, contrasting with other schools, while listing extensive occasions for ritual bathing (ghusl) beyond the primary obligation of janabah. The text underscores the practical application of divine commands in daily worship, linking physical purity to spiritual readiness.

en.dr-ali-peiravi: 26-11 Ahmad ibn Muhammad al-Haysam al-Ajali, Ahmad ibn al-Hassan al-Qat’tan, Muhammad ibn Ahmad al-Sin’ani, al-Hussein ibn Ibrahim ibn Ahmad ibn Hisham al-Mokattib, Abdullah ibn Muhammad al-Saéq and Ali ibn Abdullah al-Var’raq - may God be pleased with them - narrated that Abul Abbas Ahmad ibn Yahya ibn Zakarya al-Qattan quoted Bakr ibn Abdullah al-Habib, on the authority of Tamim ibn Buhlool, on the authority of Abu Muawiyah, on the authority of Al-A’amash that Ja’far ibn Muhammad as-Sadiq (as) said,

“These are the religious decrees. God guides whoever decides to adhere to them. Make ritual ablutions (wuzu) just as the Honorable the Exalted God has commanded in His Speaking Book. (O ye who believe! when ye prepare for prayer,) wash your faces, and your hands (and arms) to the elbows; Rub your heads (with water); and your feet to the ankles…) This is allowed once or twice.Ritual ablutions (wuzu) will only be defiled by defecation, farting, urination, ejaculation, menses and spotting. Whoever washes his feet (during ablutions) from over the slippers God, His Prophet and His Book. His ablutions are not correct and his prayer is not accepted. There are various forms of ritual bathing (ghusl) like bathing after the major ceremonial impurity (caused by sexual intercourse or the ejaculation of semen) ; wet dreams; menstruation; touching the dead after it gets cold; for having washed the dead; on Fridays; on the two Eids ; upon entering Mecca; upon entering Medina; going on pilgrimage; entering the state of ritual consecration (or Ihram); on the day of Arafat ; on the first night of the (Arabic) month of Ramazan ; on the 17th night; the 19th night;, the 21st night, and the 23rd night of Ramazan. (All these are based on traditions.) However, the ritual bathing for major ritual impurity is obligatory as is the ritual bathing for menstruation.
